# WWII Sim Master Rules sheet

Rules primarily created by Luke Jandora and Will Auman

# Important message 

It is impossible to list every single rule for the WWII sim here, everything will require some mod discretion. The future leaders of the sim should feel free to add or replace rules.

# Resources

Starting Resources and levels:  
USA= OP: OL: SP: SL: PP: PL:  
USSR= OP: OL: SP: SL: PP: PL:  
Italy= OP: OL: SP: SL: PP: PL:  
UK= OP: OL: SP: SL: PP: PL:  
Commonwealth= OP: OL: SP: SL: PP: PL:  
France= OP: OL: SP: SL: PP: PL:  
Japan= OP: OL: SP: SL: PP: PL:

There are three resources. For three of the resources, oil, steel, and population you have a “level” for each. At the start of each year, which will be announced by the moderators, you gain the number of resource points that your statsheet says you gain for that level. You gain levels for doing things that your country would historically have done. For example, if you do something good and gain the support of your people, you may level up your population. Each of the three main resources levels up independently of the other. You also have a starting value for each resource. That is how many resources you start with at the beginning of the game. You start at level 5 for each resource.

When you level up, you also receive that level’s resource number immediately after the level up.

# 

# Battles

The battle system is based on d6s (six-sided dice). In general, a “high roll” is determined to be a roll of 4, 5, or 6\. A “low roll” is a roll of 1, 2, or 3\. Before the dice are thrown, select high or low. The results of the battle. The primary way dice are calculated is based on the amount of troops brought. You may keep some amount of dice from the battle depending on how well you do. Mods should use discretion when determining how many dice a country keeps after a battle.

## Test battle system

You will have an initial roll consisting of a high-low where the country guesses whether the dice will roll high(4, 5, or 6\) or low(1, 2, or 3\) on a six sided die. The amount of dice in a battle is the amount of battle dice you brought into the battle plus the bonuses received from mod. Depending on the rolls of both parties in the participating battle, the mod will determine how many dice are lost in the initial roll. These dice are casualties. The second roll will consist of a retreating roll. This roll will be the roll of the surviving dice, and will decide how well they retreat. The number of dice in this roll are the remaining dice subtracted by the bonuses received by the winning side that will be decided by the mod based on the written battle plan. The fate of the dice that were lost in the retreat will be determined by the mod based on the battle plan written by the player. This will also be decided by a high-low roll  
Note: The point of the new system is to stop armies from vanishing, and make the number of deaths in battles more accurate. It also is meant to encourage more detailed  battle plans.

## Buying dice

Buying any infantry die costs 2 population points, 1 oil point, and 1 steel point.  
Buying any naval or air die costs 1 population point, 3 steel points, and 2 oil points  
Buying any spy die  costs 1 population point, 1 steel point, and 1 oil point. 

### Important message

Dice represent arbitrary numbers of troops, not a specific number. For example, the maginot line starts with 30 dice. Czechoslovakia starts with 2 dice.

# 

# Nuclear Weapon Rules

## Preface

Nuclear bombs are very hard for any country to obtain. It should be essentially impossible for countries outside of Russia, Germany, and The United States to obtain nuclear bombs. It should still be very difficult for any country to obtain nuclear bombs apart from the United States

## Establishing a program

To establish a nuclear program, a country must have a well thought-out plan.   
It must include  
1.The Location for the nuclear research  
2.The Location for nuclear testing  
3.Where the nuclear scientists will be obtained fr/om  
4.Where they get the resources for the nuclear program(i.e heavy water)

Do not allow a country to set up a nuclear program if they are not the United States, Russia, or Germany  
If the plan is good enough, allow them to roll a high low on three dice for the price of that country's air research. If two of the dice are correct the nuclear program will be set up.

## Bomb research

After the nuclear program is set up they must first roll to research a nuclear bomb. A roll to research a nuclear bomb costs that country's air research cost.

If they are playing the United States, have them pick a number between 1-6. After that roll a die. If the result is the number they chose, they have a nuclear bomb.

If they are Russia or Germany, have them pick a number between 1-6. After that roll three dice. If the result on both the die is the number they chose, they have a nuclear bomb

If a country fails to obtain a nuclear bomb, add a die to the roll the next time they attempt to research a nuclear bomb. Cap the number of die allowed at 3\.

There are very rare scenarios in which countries can research nuclear bombs easier than they typically can. For example, in the October 2023 sim, Russia obtained the research for Germany's nuclear program, this allowed Russia to use the United states rules for researching nukes. Whenever you think that a country should be able to research nukes, or that they should be able to research them more easily, use discretion.

After a country obtains their first nuclear bomb it should be significantly easier. Once a country obtains a nuclear bomb, researching another nuclear bomb rules are as such

If they are the United States, have them pick a high-low on one die. If they get it correct they obtain another nuclear bomb.

If they are Russia or Germany have them pick a high-low on three dice. If they get all three correct they obtain another nuclear bomb.

If a country rolls more than the required amount of correct dice for their research roll, they will be able to forgo testing. This only applies to countries that use more than one die for nuclear research.

## Nuclear testing

After a nuclear bomb is obtained, they must do nuclear testing. Nuclear testing will not consume the bomb. The rules for nuclear testing are as follows.

A country may spend their air research cost to test the nuclear bomb. The roll will be a high low on four dice, if three dice are correct the bomb works. If 1 or less dice are correct the bomb no longer works and they will have to research another bomb using the rules above. If 2 dice are correct, they can try testing the bomb again

If testing is successful, the country should be allowed to use the bomb at the beginning of the next year. If both dice are correct, the country should be allowed to use the bomb immediately.

## Nuke effects

If a country is nuked their morale immediately shoots down by 75%.  
The country also loses 7 levels of population  
The country also loses steel, oil, and additional population levels and points based on where the nuke hits.   
For example: A nuclear bomb on a major city like Tokyo would lose a significant amount of population, but not much steel and oil. A bomb dropped on a city like Manchester would lose a significant amount of steel as opposed to population(which they would still lose because they are a major city).

# Research

There are 4 different types of research costs, each having  subsections of research on their own  
Each country has their own costs for research

The 3 subsections of land research are Improved Weaponry, Tank Warfare, & more efficient movements

The 3 subsections of naval research are naval to naval battling, coastal defenses, & submarine warfare

The 4 subsections of air research are Bombing, anti aircraft, dogfighting, & nuclear bombs.

The 3 subsections of spy research are Spying evade, Spying endure, and Spying enlighten.

Some countries may begin with research already completed.  
On a failed research the country loses half of the materials put into it.

| Research Type | Effect |
| :---- | :---- |
| Tank Warfare(5 levels) | 20% more dice when infantry dice are bought |
| More efficient movement(One Level) | All oil prices are reduced by 20% for transporting troops on land & occupying territory |
| Improved Weaponry( One level) | If you pay one steel per failure, you can re-roll all extreme failures (1 or 6), once per battle |
| Naval to Naval battles(5 levels) | 20% more dice when naval dice are bought |
| Coastal Defenses(5 levels) | 20% more dice when dice are bought |
| Submarine Warfare(5 levels) | Level 1: Ability to use submarines Levels 2-5: 20% more dice when naval dice are bought |
| Bombing(5 Levels) | 20% more air  dice when dice are bought |
| Anti Aircraft( 5 levels) | When bought automatically receive Level 1: Minor anti air for cities. 50%  Number of planes attacking city=anti air die Level 2: Better city defenses and sparse anti air around the country. 50%  Number of planes attacking city=anti air die. 25% Number  of planes flying over the country’s territory=anti air. Level 3: Armies will now have mobile anti air, be able to defend from planes while on the move and away from their home countries. 25% of attacking planes= Anti air die Level 4-5: increase anti air defense rolls by 25% each level. |
| Improved Plane weaponry | If you pay one steel per  dice in battle, you can re-roll all extreme failures (1 or 6), once per battle |
| Dogfighting(5 levels) | 20% more air  dice when dice are bought |
| Nuclear research | Effects listed above |
| Spying evade(5 levels) | Level 1: Ability to use spies Level 2-5: Add a die to the total dice rolled and require one more dice to be correct to be captured(per level) |
| Spying endure(5 levels) | Add a die to the total dice rolled and require one more dice to be correct to gain information from the captured spy (per level) |
| Spying enlighten(5 levels) | Add a die to the total dice rolled and keep the same number of correct  dice to gain information from the country (per level) |

most research should happen using a 5 dice high-low. The level of research attempted should be the amount of correct dice needed for it to be successful. Most researches have a max level of 5, but some only have 1 levels.

If a country starts with research, don’t count it against them for future research levels  
For example:Germany, who starts with a level of tank research should be allowed to only have 1 die correct even though they are upgrading to level 2

# 

# Trading

Trading requires 2 or more countries to agree to exchange resources.  
For every 4 resources traded(both ways) you must pay 1 steel and 1 oil.

# Troop movement

Troop movement is standard no matter how far they are moved.   
It costs 1 oil to move any type of die  
It also costs 1 oil per year to occupy a territory that isn’t your own.

# Meetings

You can send a telegram to a country to propose a meeting to one or more countries. If that country accepts you may meet in one of the designated meeting rooms. All meetings require at least one mod present, and the only 2 countries allowed to talk without a meeting are the United Kingdom and Commonwealth.

Be careful, if your countries are at war, they may not take kindly to meetings of the two nations.

# Spy rules

A country may spend the cost of a 1PP 1SP 1OP to send a spy to another country.  
They shall have the spied on country roll a high low on 3 dice to get the spies into the country  
If the countries are strong allies, only require 1 incorrect die to get the spies into the country  
If the countries are uneasy allies, require 2 incorrect dice to get the spies into the country  
If the countries are at war, require 3 incorrect dice to get the spies into the country

Once a spy is in the country have them roll high lows of varying difficulties based on what they are trying to discover

For example, if they are trying to discover battle plans, it will be a slightly easier roll. If they are trying to discover the science for nuclear research, it will be a more difficult roll

Never let any spy discovery roll be more than 50% success rate without research.

At the beginning of every year the spied upon country rolls the initial entry high and low.  
If a spy is caught the country that catches the spy will roll to turn them. Through torture or any other means.  
The roll will be a high-low roll on 3 dice. 2 must be correct to turn the spy.

# Morale

Each country will be publicly measured on its morale, morale changes based on actions taken by the country, and you receive your morale rewards at the beginning of each year.  
The Morale ticker will be public for each team to view and goes from 1 to 100  
The effects listed below are not everything morale can do, leave it up to some mod decisions.  
A Morale of 0 will result in riots and the army being relatively unwilling to fight for your country  
Morale from 0-20 loses a country a level of everything per year  
Morale from 21-40 loses 5 of each resource per year  
Morale from 41-60 stays the same per year  
Morale from 61-80 gains 5 of each resource per year  
Morale from 81-100 gains a country a level of everything per year  
**United States Starting:10**  
**United Kingdom Starting:60**  
**Commonwealth Starting:50**  
**Russia Starting:65**  
**France Starting:70**  
**Germany Starting:90**  
**Japan Starting:80**  
**Italy Starting:50**

# Miscellaneous

# Scrap metal drives

A country may do a scrap metal drive once a year a total of 3 times  
The first time roll 4d6 and give them that number of steel  
Second time roll 2d6  
Third time roll 1d6

# Historical Rolls

## Japan

Japan will receive a roll for war crimes in China leading up to 1941\. A high-low for war crimes if unsuccessful nothing happens. If unsuccessful then troops have committed war crimes in china and other countries can act on the unfavorable position of war crimes.
